setup.platform.title: Where is your chat?
setup.platform.hint: Pick the service your viewers are watching on. You can use both at once.
setup.twitch.title: Twitch channel
setup.twitch.hint: Your Twitch username. The app only reads chat — it can never post as you, and no password or token is involved.
setup.youtube.title: YouTube channel
setup.youtube.hint: Your handle, channel link or the link to the live stream. The app finds the running broadcast by itself.
setup.steps.title: How to play
setup.steps.2: Start your game, then pick it under Settings so chat cannot type anywhere else.
setup.steps.3: Press Start in the top corner.
setup.steps.4: Click into the game so it is the active window. Chat is now in control.
setup.panic.title: Panic button
setup.panic.body: Press {key} anywhere, even mid-game, to pause everything and release every held key. Press it again to carry on.
setup.overlay.title: Overlay for OBS
setup.overlay.hint: A sign on your stream telling viewers what they can type. Every command is shown at once, and it updates itself whenever you change something here.
setup.overlay.obs: In OBS: Sources → + → Browser, paste the address, width {width}, height {height}. Set the height generously — the sign only takes the room it needs and the background is transparent.
commands.title: Commands
commands.hint: What chat types, and what happens in the game. Click the key box and press a key to record it — hold two down together for a combination. Press {icon} to try a command in whatever window is in front.
commands.hint.info: The explanation under each line is what viewers read on the overlay, and the switches beside it change how the command behaves.
commands.empty: No commands yet. Add your first one below.
commands.holdTitle: Set 1 second or more and chat can choose how long
commands.tested: Tried "{name}" in the window in front
commands.duplicateName: There is already a command with that name
commands.modOnly.title: Only moderators and you can trigger this
commands.hidden.title: Whether this command is listed on the overlay. Hidden ones still work — chat just has to know they exist.
commands.override.title: Chat wins: whatever you are holding is released, and your own presses of the profile's keys are ignored for as long as the command runs.
commands.hold.title: Let chat type a number after the command to hold the key down, e.g. "forward 2".
commands.holdMax.title: The longest chat may hold this key, in seconds.
commands.repeat.title: Press the key several times in a row instead of holding it. A command either holds or repeats, never both.
commands.repeatCount.title: How many presses, and the most chat may ask for.
commands.repeatInterval.title: Seconds between each press.
commands.problem.repeatTooFew: repeat is on but set to fewer than two presses
overlay.repeatHint: Choose how many times by adding a number: {example}
commands.length.title: How long the key is held for an ordinary press, in seconds.
commands.problem.holdWithoutLimit: hold is on but has no limit
commands.holdTip.title: Holding and repeating
commands.holdTip.body: Turn on Hold and chat can type {example} to hold the key for two seconds, up to the limit you set. Turn on Repeat instead and the same number means how many presses. A command does one or the other, so the number is never ambiguous.
settings.mode.title: How chat plays
settings.mode.hint: Anarchy is the most fun with a busy chat. Voting suits calm games, puzzles and Pokémon.
settings.mode.anarchy.help: Every message becomes a key press straight away.
settings.mode.democracy.help: Chat votes, and the most popular command wins.
settings.vote.label: How long can chat vote?
settings.rate.label: How fast are commands carried out?
settings.rate.help: Lower means more chaos. Higher is calmer and easier to follow.
settings.window.title: Only this game
settings.window.hint: Pick your game's window so chat's key presses land there and nowhere else — not in Discord, your browser or OBS. Strongly recommended.
settings.limits.title: Keeping chat in check
settings.cooldown.label: Wait between each viewer's commands
settings.queue.label: How many commands may wait in line
settings.queue.help: A low number keeps the game close to real time.
settings.app.title: App
settings.language.label: Language
settings.overlayPort.label: Overlay port
settings.overlayPort.help: Only change this if another program is already using the port.
look.colours.title: Colours
look.colours.hint: These apply to both overlays, so the command list and the poll always match.
look.shape.title: Shape and size
look.parts.title: What to show
look.preview.title: Preview
look.preview.hint: The real overlay pages, exactly as OBS will load them. The chequerboard is the transparent background.
look.preview.pollIdle: The poll overlay stays invisible until a poll is running.
profile.label: Profile
profile.deleteBody: This cannot be undone. Export it first if you want to keep a copy.
profile.deleteLast: You cannot delete your only profile.
profile.importFailed: That file is not a profile the app can read.
profile.importNoCommands: That profile has no commands in it.
help.notWorking.title: The game is not reacting
help.notWorking.admin.head: Nothing happens in the game:
help.notWorking.admin.body: Close Streamthings, right-click it and choose Run as administrator. Some games run with administrator rights, and Windows blocks key presses sent from ordinary programs.
help.notWorking.fullscreen.head: Works in the menu but not in the game:
help.notWorking.fullscreen.body: Switch the game to borderless window instead of exclusive fullscreen.
help.notWorking.delay.head: Chat reacts a few seconds late:
help.notWorking.delay.body: That is your stream delay — viewers see the picture after it happens. Turn on low latency mode in your Twitch or YouTube settings to shrink it.
help.notWorking.nothing.head: Nothing happens at all:
help.notWorking.nothing.body: Check the channel name is spelled right and that the top of the window says Connected.
help.anticheat.title: Important: anti-cheat
help.anticheat.body: Do not use this in competitive games such as Valorant, CS2, Fortnite or Rainbow Six. Automated input can get the account banned. Single-player games, emulators, Minecraft and silly games are where this belongs.
help.profiles.title: Profiles
help.profiles.body: Each profile keeps its own commands and settings, so you can switch between games in one click. Export a profile to share it with someone, or import one they sent you.
help.hidden.title: Hidden commands and overrides
help.hidden.body: The eye beside a command decides whether it appears on the overlay. A hidden command still works exactly as normal — handy for a secret one you tell chat about yourself, or for keeping a long list readable. Override is the mischievous one: it lets go of whatever you are holding and then ignores your own presses until the command finishes, so you cannot simply out-mash chat.
help.override.title: Override and your antivirus
help.override.body: Ignoring your own key presses needs a Windows feature that antivirus software watches closely, because keyloggers use the same one. Streamthings only ever asks it one question — whether this exact key is suppressed right now — and it is switched on only while a profile has an overriding command and chat is playing. Nothing is recorded and nothing is sent anywhere. If your antivirus complains anyway, that is why; turn Override off on every command and the feature is never switched on at all.
help.poll.title: Polls
help.poll.body: A poll is its own thing, separate from chat playing the game. You can run one whether or not chat is in control, and it never blocks them — if a vote word is also a command, both happen, and the app warns you when that is the case. The poll has its own browser source, so put it wherever suits your scene.
help.overlays.title: The two overlays
help.overlays.body: The command list lives at the address on the Get started page, and the poll at that same address with /poll on the end. Add them as separate browser sources in OBS. The poll one draws nothing at all until a poll is running, so it can sit in your scene permanently.
help.privacy.title: What the app can and cannot do
help.privacy.body: Streamthings reads chat as an anonymous viewer. It cannot post messages, it never asks for your Twitch or YouTube password or a token, and nothing leaves your computer except the request to read chat. If you turn on Lights, it also talks to OBS and to your Nanoleaf on your own network — nothing else.

poll.hint: Put a question to chat and let them answer by typing. This runs on its own — it does not need chat to be playing, and it never gets in the way if they are.

poll.duration.label: How long can they vote?

poll.clash.many: Chat typing {keys} will also fire those game commands. Both happen — rename the options if you would rather they did not.

overlay.sub.anarchy: Type a command in chat — it happens straight away.
overlay.sub.democracy: Type a command in chat. Every {seconds} seconds the most voted one wins.

lights.obs.title: OBS
lights.obs.hint: Your Nanoleaf light can change along with the scene you switch to in OBS. In OBS 28 or newer, open Tools → WebSocket Server Settings, tick Enable WebSocket server, and copy the password from Show Connect Info. Streamthings only listens — it never changes anything in OBS.
lights.obs.password.placeholder: leave empty if OBS has none
lights.obs.status.disabled: Off — the light does not follow OBS
lights.obs.status.idle: Off — the light does not follow OBS
lights.obs.status.offline: OBS is not answering at {host}. Is it running? Trying again in the background.
lights.obs.status.needPassword: OBS asks for a password — enter it above
lights.obs.status.unsupported: This OBS is too old. OBS 28 or newer is needed.
lights.nanoleaf.title: Nanoleaf
lights.nanoleaf.hint: The light and this PC must be on the same network. Type the light's IP address — you find it in your router, or in the Nanoleaf app under the device — or press Search.
lights.nanoleaf.noneFound: No Nanoleaf found on the network. Type its IP address instead.
lights.nanoleaf.status.offline: {name} is not answering. Is it switched on and on the same network?
lights.nanoleaf.status.timeout: {name} is not answering. Is it switched on and on the same network?
lights.nanoleaf.status.unauthorized: {name} no longer accepts this pairing. Pair it again.
lights.nanoleaf.status.badResponse: {name} gave an answer the app did not understand
lights.pair.title: Hold the power button now
lights.pair.body: Press and hold the on/off button on the Nanoleaf controller for 5–7 seconds, until the lights start to flash. The app is listening.
lights.pair.timeout: The light never went into pairing mode. Hold the button a little longer and try again.
lights.pair.offline: Nothing answered at that address. Check the IP address.
lights.pair.badAddress: Type the light's IP address first
lights.forget.title: Forget this light?
lights.forget.body: Your scene choices are kept. To use the light again you will need to pair it again.
lights.scenes.title: Scenes
lights.scenes.hint: Choose what the light does when each scene goes on air. A scene left blank changes nothing. The ▶ button tries a row on the light straight away.
lights.scenes.empty: Turn on OBS above and your scenes appear here.
lights.scenes.waiting: Waiting for OBS to list its scenes…
lights.chip.off.title: Turn the light off when this scene goes on air
lights.clear.title: Clear this scene
lights.last.failed: Could not change the light for {scene}: {reason}
lights.error.notFound: that effect is no longer on the light
lights.error.badResponse: the light gave an unexpected answer
lights.error.nothingToDo: choose an effect, a brightness or Off first
help.lights.title: Lights that follow OBS
help.lights.body: On the Lights page, Streamthings can listen to OBS and change your Nanoleaf light whenever you switch scene — a calm effect for Starting soon, off for Be right back, full brightness for the game. It is one setup for the whole stream, whichever profile is active. If OBS or the light is switched off, nothing else in the app is affected: the page just says so and keeps trying.
